title_o: Silence is Golden: Effect of Encouragement in Motivating the Weak Link in an Online Exercise Video Game

replications.journal: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
replications.quote: Newly collected data corroborated Irwin et al.’s (2013) finding that encouragement using the ambiguous and exclusive pronoun “you” (e.g. “you can do it”) from a virtually present partner significantly weakened this Köhler effect. Some partial support was found for Irwin et al.’s expla- nation of this effect. Irwin et al. suggested that when one hears one’s partner say things like “you can do it!”, that may be interpreted that the partner is him/herself struggling and is to some degree trying to encourage him/herself. Hence, that partner may not be as superior as previously thought.

effect.name: Partner encouragement attenuates the Köhler exercise gain
